source.title: String Quartet in F major — II. Assez vif — Très rythmé
source.edition: OpenScore String Quartets; transcribed from IMSLP #335585

musicxmlFlattenTuplets.basis: The source viola has 36 sixteenths per bar in nested 3:2 quarter and 6:4 sixteenth tuplets, explicitly combined as 18:8 in time-modification. Each note is exactly 1/9 quarter; flatten only the nested brackets and represent the rational duration exactly, preserving pitches, order, beaming and slurs.

musicxmlTieRoutes.basis: The original viola bar 88 encodes simultaneous identical dotted-half A4 notes in voices 1 and 4 at q261; only voice 4 carries the outgoing tie, while bar 89’s first A4 at q264 carries its stop in voice 1. Route only that explicit tie start onto the identical voice-1 unison so the written continuation ends at q265 without an invented reattack at q264. Preserve both original notes, their onsets and durations, and the voice-4 inverted fermata; change only tie ownership in a disposable derivative.

musicxmlTrillSpans.basis: Native violin-I trill ends at II.10 quarter 1, where the next trill starts. The MusicXML stop is at the end of a hidden voice-4 cue; retain the hidden cue and route only its ornament stop to the existing voice-1 onset.
Native violin-I trill ends at II.11 quarter 1, where the next trill starts. The MusicXML stop is at the end of a hidden voice-4 cue; preserve that cue's visibility and all timed notes.

Native violin-I next-location advances two measures minus one quarter from II.11 quarter 1, ending at II.13 quarter 0. The original stop belongs to the end of the hidden voice-3 rest in II.12, not its onset.
Native violin-I trill spans II.50–51 and ends at II.52 quarter 0. Preserve the hidden voice-3 rest carrying the exported stop and route only that stop to its source-defined ending in voice 1.

Native violin-I trill starts at II.160 quarter 0.5 and ends two measures minus half a quarter later, at II.162 quarter 0. The voice-2 rest's exported stop is an end-of-rest position, not an attack or a duration change.
Native viola E-flat5 trill lasts half a whole-note unit, ending at II.175 quarter 2 as the D5 trill begins. Keep the hidden voice-2 rest and place only its stop at the existing voice-1 D5 onset.

Native viola D5 trill advances one measure minus one quarter, ending at II.176 quarter 1. Preserve the written auxiliary D-sharp5 and route only its exported end-of-note stop to the voice-1 C-sharp5 onset.

MusicXML export omits this stop. The immutable native MSCX explicitly advances one measure minus one quarter from II.176 quarter 1 to II.177 quarter 0, with a reciprocal previous-location entry there; the companion viola PDF page 8 shows the same bounded C-sharp5 trill before B4. Restore only that source-proven stop at the existing voice-1 B4 onset, not a guessed duration.
Native viola B4 trill spans II.177–178 and ends before the pizzicato passage at II.179 quarter 0. The existing voice-1 quarter rest provides that exact stop position; no timed event or note is added.

bars.description: Movement II only: bars 1–198 once in written order. No repeat signs occur in the selected MusicXML; thematic returns are written out.

endpoints.basis: Opening A4/E4/A3 pizzicato occurs around 0.25 s; the stronger same-pitch entry around 2.54 s is a later repetition, not the beginning. The final pizzicato sonority occurs around 346.55 s after the preceding arpeggiated bars, not the earlier chord around 342.94 s. The final window includes the actual attack rather than its later 346.9 s decay. These source-pitch windows prevent collapsing the first three and final three bars onto repeated harmonies. Numerical and visual inspection only; no aural review is claimed.

anchors.label: bar-196-pre-final-chord
anchors.basis: Source bar 196 begins at q591 with B-flat3/D4/A4/E5/E6, after the second C6–D6 rise at q590/590.5. Individual pitch bands locate that rise around 342.5/342.7 s and the A4/E6/B-flat3 arrival around 342.9 s. An unconstrained numerical pass placed q591 near 343.64 s, over already decayed upper-pitch energy, stretching the preceding run across the written pause. This measured source-pitch alignment constraint restores the chord before the pause; it is not independent validation and does not replace any numerical gate or the genuine final q597.5 attack.

provenance: Select zero-based half-open MusicXML measure indices [213, 411] from every part, preserving inherited clefs, keys and time signatures. Original CC0 MXL download remains unchanged.
Four source-defined instrument parts are retained, including all explicitly encoded subsidiary voices within each staff. MIDI articulations are not used to invent performed note lengths.
Metric-equivalence instructions and textual dynamics require semantics-preserving conversion to text for LilyPond 2.24.4; no note or rhythmic content is removed.

Viola bars 120–123 require an explicit nested-tuplet derivative because musicxml2ly duplicated their note groups. The source’s written sixteenth type and combined 18:8 ratio determine 1/9-quarter notes, despite rounded XML durations of 53/480. Exact rational rescaling and equivalent flat 18:8 brackets preserve all 36 notes per bar; the four-part 600-quarter bar grid is not enlarged to accommodate the converter defect.

The separately pinned original OpenScore MSCX preserves all nine complete trill spanners. In movement-II quarter units, violin I spans are 25–28, 28–31, 31–36, 147–153 and 483.5–489; viola spans are 528–530, 530–532, 532–534 and 534–540. Native Staff 3, zero-based measure index 388, explicitly sends the C-sharp trill at II.176 quarter 1 to the next measure minus one quarter: II.177 quarter 0, q534. This resolves the stop omitted by MusicXML export without inventing an ornament duration. Visible written trill auxiliary/cue notes remain source notation, not claimed independent physical reattacks.
